minutes.headline: Design committee previewed the Town Hall/Ritter/Meeting House plan and cost estimate ahead of the Select Board; minutes approved.
minutes.summary: The Municipal Building Design Committee heard Taylor and Burns and its engineers present the site plan, floor plans, renderings, structural and MEP systems and a newly finalized cost estimate, as a preview of the next night's Select Board presentation. Discussion covered parking, generator and EV charger questions, and a lengthy debate over whether the project is sellable to voters at town meeting. The committee approved two sets of prior minutes, set a rescheduled meeting date, and adjourned.

public_comment.topic: Mr Walker (PAC) asked that any PAC-specific items be squeezed in early because he had to leave at 6.

Parking: argued 80 spaces is not enough for the town center and urged the committee to look at adding more; also asked about the Old Town Hall basement foundation and moisture, advising against fully sealing the floor.

votes.motion: Approve the meeting minutes of January 6 and January 22, by roll call.
votes.outcome: approved; roll call yeas heard from Roy, Gray, Scullen Bini and chair; Mr Blat abstained
passed; all roll call responses were ayes

budget_items.topic: Construction cost per square foot / 1965 Ritter addition value
budget_items.what_was_said: Architect said new construction cost estimate is almost $600 a square foot, so the roughly 1500 sq ft 1965 addition is worth about $900,000 of real estate to be reused.
Trade costs given for Meeting House, Ritter, Town Hall and site work, totaling about 13.3 million.

budget_items.topic: Contingency, escalation and total construction cost
budget_items.what_was_said: Design contingencies and a one-year escalation were added to reach the total estimated construction cost.
With design fees and owner's project manager at a 20 or 25 percent margin, total project cost is in the low 20 millions.

budget_items.topic: Alternates: PV canopy, basement slab, EV chargers
budget_items.what_was_said: Three alternates are excluded from the estimate; no federal rebates were estimated.

A member cited the solar canopy alternate and asked about green grants; the Green Committee chair said community solar grants are possible but harder, and heat pump grants easier. No grant or rebate was programmed into the estimate.

budget_items.topic: EV charger rough-in in site work
budget_items.what_was_said: Conduit and rough-in for the chargers is code-required and included in site work, while the chargers themselves are priced separately.
The estimate carries a bare-bones basement, with the PAC expected to fund its own outfitting.

budget_items.topic: Overall project price and PAC add
budget_items.what_was_said: The APDC rep said a project of this size must be strongly supported by voters and objected to adding PAC, citing an added cost.
Chair said four price points are in play and the committee must settle article wording to borrow at the March 17 meeting.

decisions.decision: The February 17 meeting, falling on Presidents Day, is to be moved to February 19, pending confirmation with absent members.
The March 17 meeting will be used to confirm the wording of the borrowing warrant article, with the committee to come prepared on which price option to pursue.

Chair will present to the Finance Committee and Council on Aging (on the 11th) and follow up with the Historical Commission and Planning Board; Mr Blat asked to research available grant opportunities.
Architect team to quickly get a price for a generator as a possible alternate, after discussion that none is code-required.
Architect to send the latest design drawings; the cost estimate had already been distributed.
Presentation to the Select Board set for the next evening at Town Hall, appointment at 7:15 in a 45-minute slot, roughly a 20-25 minute presentation.

what_happened.line: The Municipal Building Design Committee previewed the Town Hall, Ritter and Meeting House plan and a newly finalized cost estimate ahead of the next night's Select Board presentation.
The committee set March 17 to confirm the wording of a borrowing warrant article and to come prepared on which of four price options to pursue.
The committee debated at length whether the project can be sold to voters at town meeting, including adding the performing arts center, and reached no resolution.
The architect team is to price a generator as a possible alternate, since none is code-required; the estimate leaves out three alternates and assumes no grants or rebates.
The February 17 meeting, which falls on Presidents Day, is to move to February 19, pending confirmation with absent members; the committee approved two sets of prior minutes.

why_it_matters: The total project cost was described as in the low twenties of millions, and the borrowing article is the vote residents would be asked to take at town meeting, so the price option chosen on March 17 sets the debt behind it.
The estimate leaves out grants, rebates and the solar canopy, EV chargers and basement slab alternates, so the figure a voter sees may change depending on what is added or funded elsewhere.
